slot.brief: Given average bond enthalpies of all bonds broken and formed, compute the enthalpy of reaction for a simple gas-phase reaction.

stem: For $\text{H}_2(g)+\text{Cl}_2(g)\rightarrow 2\text{HCl}(g)$, the mean bond enthalpies are H–H $436$, Cl–Cl $243$ and H–Cl $431\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Find $\Delta H$.

verdicts.working: Bonds broken: 436 + 243 = 679 kJ mol⁻¹. Bonds formed: 2(431) = 862 kJ mol⁻¹. Thus ΔH = 679 − 862 = −183 kJ mol⁻¹.

working:
$\Delta H=\sum D(\text{broken})-\sum D(\text{formed})$
$=(436+243)-2(431)=-183\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
